content: Introduction s allow you to create a series of forward-looking, scheduled s based on criteria you define through our EZ preset or advanced fields. You can: Relate the to any object (standard/custom). Auto capture payments. Capture a valid through the terminal that updates all related s. Automatically request payment through . Create an advanced for unique due dates. Parent Object Relationship s are related to the parent object(s) you defined in the Blackthorn | Payments Setup Wizard . Each parent object has a lookup field automatically created and placed on the 's page layout. This allows you to relate your parent object(s) to your and to add the s to your parent object(s). s out-of-the-box have lookups (relationships) to both the and objects. Just add the to your and/or page layouts. Create an EZ Preset Payment Schedule The EZ Preset process is used for creating simple s. Navigate to our object. Lightning: Click the App Launcher > In the search box enter and click Payment Schedules. Classic: Click on "All Tabs" ("+" icon in the top right) > Click Payment Schedules. Click . Populate required and optional fields. The best feature of our Payment Schedule object is the ability to mix and match the fields you enter for generating scheduled Transactions. There are certain required fields (not marked required on the page layout) that need to be filled in when creating an "EZ Preset" Payment Schedule. Required Fields : This field determines the frequency of each with its . : This date determines when the should start. This date can be the first 's , or the subsequent 's if the first was captured immediately. or : Either of these fields will determine the number of s that need to be created. or : Either of these fields will determine the amount of each . Optional Fields : The first 's (for example, initial fee + monthly amount) may be different than the other recurring payments. If you use this field, only enter OR , not both. : Add the customer's related if you want to automatically process the generated s based on its . You can also use our feature. Then you would leave the field blank and request payment through one of the 's s. The remaining picklist values are automatically set based on the status of the related s. To generate the s for your , the must be set to "Generate". That triggers the system to create all s based on your 's EZ Preset and/or advanced fields. You can also generate the Payment Schedule by clicking Generate , located in the upper right corner of the Payment Schedule record page. : This field is updated automatically. Once related s are created, each one will auto-process based on their . A valid is needed in order to auto-process the . See our Transaction documentation for more information. Click . Create an Advanced Payment Schedule There are additional use cases where the 's frequency needs to be more complex than what is provided in the "EZ Preset" fields. For those use cases, you should use the advanced fields. First, enter all of the required and optional fields listed above with the exception of the EZ Preset field. That field will be replaced by the advanced schedule fields. For example, if your needs to capture a payment once every three weeks, you would use our advanced schedule fields. = "Weekly" = "3" The result will show that each 's will be three weeks apart. As you can see in the below images, a was created using the advanced fields and instead of the EZ Preset field since a payment needed to be captured every three weeks. Keep in mind, if you did not add a valid or requested a payment through , the related s will NOT capture a payment from your customer. Open-ended Payment Schedules Open-Ended s are single amounts captured over and over again, with no ending date defined. The will continue until you close it. The field defines the type of open-ended you want. Blank Field = The is not open-ended and will end after the number of completed s matches the . "Keep One Open" = After one is completed, another open is generated on the same frequency. "Auto-Renew" = After all initial s are completed, the will generate the full again. For example, if there were 12 original s, there will be 12 new future s. Default the number of initial transactions created... There is a custom setting that allows you to define the default number of Transactions to be created for "Keep One Open" and "Auto-Renew" options. The current default is 12 Transactions. Navigate to Custom Settings > click Manage next to Blackthorn Pay - Trigger Settings > update the default "Payment Schedule Transaction Count". Keep One Open Example : "Monthly" : "Keep One Open" : "2" This means that there will always be two open s. Auto-Renew Example : "Monthly" : "Auto-Renew" : "2" This means that after the two s are completed, two more will automatically generate. **If you didn't set the , 12 s would automatically be created based on the default custom setting. Schedule and Payment Statuses Schedule Status Completed  The sum of all s’ equals the ’s , AND there are no open s remaining. Failed  There is a with set to “Failed” that has no available reattempts. Active  The related s have at least one with the set to “Open,” and no s with the set to “Canceled,” OR there are s with a on or before today.  Future  There are s with the set to “Open,” and none of them have the set to “Captured.” Canceled and Refunded  All s with set to “Completed” are refunded, and the remaining s with = “Open” are canceled. Canceled  All remaining s have the set to “Canceled,” and there is a Cancel  button on the record. Payment Status Failed to Collect  The failed, and there are no available reattempts or refunds. OR the was canceled and had no s with the set to “Captured” or “Refunded.” Scheduled  There are open s. And there are no s with the set to “Open” or “Canceled” or the set to “Captured” or “Refunded,” or an unpaid with a before the current date. Overdue  An open has a in the past.  Partially Paid  The sum of all s’ is greater than 0 and less than the 's . There are no refunded s or open s left to be captured.  Refunded  The sum of the related s' amount paid is zero ( = "0"), and there are no refunds or open s left to be captured. Partially Refunded  The sum of all s’ is greater than 0 and less than the 's . There is a refunded , but there are no open s left to be captured. Paid  The sum of all s’ is greater than or equal to the 's , and there are no open s left to be captured. Good Standing  There is at least one with set to “Captured.” Canceled  There are no s with the set to “Open” or set to “Captured” or “Refunded,” but there is at least one with set to “Canceled.” Matrix Once you have read through the definitions above, review the Payment Schedule Status Matrix to see how the and  fields interact.   Your browser does not support PDF.click here to download   Update a Payment Schedule There are times when you might want to update your . This may occur when a has changed in your org or maybe you need to swap out a for future "Open" s. Navigate to your existing record. Update the field to the updated value. Notice that the related s with a = "Open" are updated to include the new value. NOTE: An error message will pop up on save if you have already associated the with a from a different . This ensures that the associated s don't fail later due to mismatches. Can I pause a Payment Schedule? No. Out of the box, we don't offer an option to pause a Payment Schedule. To stop the Payment Schedule, you must cancel or delete the Payment Schedule and redo it when you need to restart it. Cancel a Payment Schedule When a is canceled, the status on the will be set to "Canceled" and the of all open and related s will also be updated to "Canceled". Use any of the below options to cancel an active . Click the Cancel button to cancel the . There is a hidden (off the page layout) checkbox field (label: ) on the object. Check this checkbox using automation logic (Workflow, Process Builder, or Flow) to cancel the . Delete a Payment Schedule When deleting a record, all related "Open" s will also be deleted. Any s with a other than "Open" will not be deleted and will continue to be related to the parent record (ie , , Custom Object, etc...) Changes to Payment Schedules There are only certain changes that will sync between Payment Schedules and the associated Transactions after the initial creation of Transaction records. Those changes are described in the Roll-up/Roll-down Features section below. If you need to make changes related to the Payment Schedule dates or amounts, we recommend canceling the current Payment Schedule and creating a new one. Roll-up/Roll-down Features Payment Method From the Updating the updates all related s with the = "Open". For example, if a customer wants to change their at any time during the schedule, update the field and the remaining "Open" s will be updated. From the Related Updates to the on a with the = "Open" are rolled up to the related . They are then rolled down to all other related "Open" s. For example, if a customer updates their through PayLink on one , all other related s and the 's will be updated. If you don't want this to occur, set the 's field to "True".
